sourceTitle: Why Nobody Can Afford a House Anymore
title: A House Used To Cost 2 Years Of Income
hook: A house once cost two years of income. Not anymore.
question: What's the ratio where you live?

sources.name: Median Sales Price of Houses Sold (FRED)
sources.quote: Median Sales Price of Houses Sold

scenes.narration: A generation ago, a house cost about two years of a normal income. Today that simple math is completely broken.
Back in nineteen seventy, the typical home cost roughly two years of the typical income. Today it is closer to six years of pay.

shots.kicker: Years of income for the typical home
shots.sub: the typical home vs a year's pay

scenes.narration: Here is the problem. Adjusted for inflation, the typical household income barely crawled upward.
But over the same stretch, the price of a home went almost straight up.
The Case-Shiller index tells the exact same story, a near-relentless climb for decades.
Put a number on it, and the median American home now costs about four hundred twelve thousand dollars.
Which is why, by one estimate, only about one in seven renters can actually afford to buy that median home.

shots.label: renters who can afford a median home

scenes.narration: So what is the price-to-income ratio where you live, and is it any better?
